column1: # Forever's own areas, and which of them have an entry.
# Every column here comes from the game's own AreaTable, fetched as CSV from
# wago.tools, whose robots.txt permits exactly that route and blocks the HTML
# browser. Product "wowf", build 1.60.1.70862, read on 2026-11-08. The names
# are the client's own spelling, which is what Data/Schema.lua keys on.
# No notes column, for the same reason tools/characters.tsv has none: the one
# in places.tsv held three wrong notes and those errors reached finished lore.
# has_entry was produced by loading the addon against tools/mock_wow.lua,
# dumping every registered entry name through ns.EachEntry, and matching on a
# normalised name. That is a name match, not the resolver: a place whose entry
# exists but whose parent zone differs would show as having one. /ftn areas
# inside the game uses the real ns.FindZone / ns.FindSub / ns.FindInstance.
# 68 areas, 49 written up, 19 to go. Counted with aliases; a name-only
# check had reported four of them wrongly.
# RE-CHECKED 2026-11-09, five days after the patch. The wiki has grown a
# Category:Riverglades subzones with ten pages in it, three of which were new:
# Ashwood's Fall, Terral's Watch and Wheeler's Grange. All three are now
# written up. Shen'dralas subzones still holds only the Valley of Bones, and
# Category:Zephras Isle still holds four pages. Mount Hyjal's subzone category
# is the retail zone's, full of Firelands and Molten Front material rather than
# Forever's. So the wiki IS filling in, zone by zone, and this is worth
# re-running every so often rather than treating as settled.
# The 35 still open are not blocked on sources any more. Martin cleared the
# built-in browser for reading warcraft.wiki.gg, whose robots.txt allows
# User-agent: * even though it names this tooling's crawler agents, and the
# zone articles carry real history. The four zone pages were read on
# 2026-11-09 and everything they support has been written.
# What is left needs the individual subzone articles, one page each, or the
# game. Client data will never supply it: quest text and NPC dialogue are what
# describe a place and both live on the server. Nine DB2 tables were checked
# through wago.tools and none of them carry a word of it, AreaPOI's 150
# descriptions being UI strings like "Alliance Controlled".
# Note the spellings can differ. The wiki calls it Evenshade Overlook; the
# client's AreaTable says Evenshade's Overlook, and the client wins, because
# GetSubZoneText is what the addon matches on.
# /ftn areas does the has_entry check from inside the game, for the whole world
